title: Some things just aren't right
takeaway: A gentle list of things a good person doesn't do.
scene: This ghazal is printed in two columns, and every couplet ends with the same phrase: 'it isn't good.' It reads like a list of advice, sometimes to the beloved, sometimes to everyone.

original: ہر اک تے وس جانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
ریت دے محل بنانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Har ik te vas jaana beeba changa nahin
Ret de mehal banaana beeba changa nahin
translation: Falling for everyone you meet isn't good, dear.
Building palaces out of sand isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: Don't fall for every person you meet. And don't build your hopes on something that won't hold, like a palace made of sand.

original: انج تے شرم حیا وی ہوندی چنگی اے
اوہلیوں تیر چلانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Inj te sharm hayaa vi hondi changi ae
Ohleyon teer chalaana beeba changa nahin
translation: Modesty and shyness are good, of course,
but shooting arrows from behind a screen isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: Being modest and shy is fine. But hiding behind it while you hurt people with sneaky glances isn't fair.

original: شوخیاں تے انگڑائیاں ٹوہر جوانی دے
لنگھدیاں اگاں لانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Shokhiyaan te angraaiyaan, tohr jawaani de
Langhdiyaan aggaan laana beeba changa nahin
translation: Playfulness and stretching, the swagger of youth:
setting fires as you walk past isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: Being young, playful and confident is natural. But walking past people and setting their hearts on fire on purpose isn't kind.

original: ہار شنگار بناں وی چنگے لگدے او
ایویں بھار اٹھانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Haar shingaar binaa vi change lagde o
Aiven bhaar uthaana beeba changa nahin
translation: You look lovely even without jewellery and make-up;
carrying all that weight for nothing isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: He tells the beloved: you look beautiful without all the jewellery and make-up. You don't need to weigh yourself down with it.

original: جھلک دکھا کے سوہنے پھل جیہے مکھڑے دی
سولاں تے ٹنگ جانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Jhalak dikha ke sohne phull jehe mukhre di
Soolaan te tang jaana beeba changa nahin
translation: Showing a glimpse of your lovely, flower-like face,
and then leaving me hung on thorns, isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: Letting someone see your beautiful face for a moment, then leaving them hanging in pain, isn't fair.

original: آس دا مندر ڈھا کے پیار دی گلی نوں
سنجا کر کے جانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Aas da mandar dha ke pyaar di gali nu
Sunja kar ke jaana beeba changa nahin
translation: Knocking down the temple of hope,
and leaving love's street empty, isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: Tearing down someone's hopes, then walking away and leaving the street of love empty, isn't right.

original: تھل دی ریت چناں دا پانی کہندا اے
عشق دا روگ لگانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Thal di ret Chanaan da paani kehnda ae
Ishq da rog lagaana beeba changa nahin
translation: The desert sand and the Chenab's water both say:
catching the sickness of love isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: The desert sand and the river Chenab have seen many lovers suffer, from the Punjabi love stories. They both warn: don't catch the 'disease' of love.

original: ظلم ستم دا تسبہ کھولیو عالم توں
بھکھیاں توں کھو کھانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Zulm sitam da tasma kholeyo aalim ton
Bhukhiyaan ton kho khaana beeba changa nahin
translation: Learned one, loosen the noose of cruelty and oppression:
snatching food from the hungry isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: He turns to people with learning and power. Stop being cruel. Taking food from hungry people is wrong.

original: پیراں وچ نہ دل دیاں کرچاں چبھ جاون
شیشہ توڑ کے جانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Pairaan vich na dil diyaan kirchaan chubh jaavan
Sheesha tor ke jaana beeba changa nahin
translation: Careful the splinters of a heart don't pierce your own feet:
smashing the glass and walking away isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: A broken heart is like broken glass. If you smash it and walk off, the sharp pieces might end up cutting your own feet.

original: من میرے وچ پیاری تیری مورت اے
پیار دا مندر ڈھانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Man mere vich pyaari teri moorat ae
Pyaar da mandar dhaana beeba changa nahin
translation: Your dear image lives in my heart:
tearing down the temple of love isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: The beloved's picture lives inside his heart, like an image in a temple. Destroying that temple would be wrong.

original: دل دے محرم باجھوں احمدؔ ہر اگے
رونا تے کرلانا بیبا چنگا نئیں
transliteration: Dil de mehram baajhon Ahmad har agge
Rona te karlaana beeba changa nahin
translation: Ahmad, in front of anyone except the one who knows your heart,
crying and wailing isn't good, dear.
couplets.story: He ends with advice for himself. Don't cry in front of just anyone, Ahmad. Save your tears for the one person who truly understands your heart.

deeper: The last couplet has a Sufi echo: pour out your heart only to the one who truly knows it. For a believer, that means bringing your grief to God, not complaining to everyone. The couplet about snatching food from the hungry is a direct moral teaching found throughout Islam.
why: The repeated ending, 'it isn't good', makes it easy to follow and fun to read aloud. It mixes flirtatious advice with serious lessons about kindness.
prompt: If you wrote your own 'it isn't good' list for how people treat each other, what would be on it?
notes: 'Beeba' is an affectionate Punjabi address, roughly 'dear' or 'good one'.
Printed in two columns; each row is read as one couplet.
